findings.defect: The interrupted request is reversed into an order for Jin Taekyung to die. Go Se-won is beginning to ask Jin to kill him, continuing their agreement.
findings.rationale: The preceding condition was that Jin kill Go Se-won after receiving the location of Area A. The omitted continuation after 죽 is therefore 죽여 달라, not a command for Jin to die.

findings.defect: The second sentence adds that Jin has already arrived, while the source only emphasizes that he is coming.
findings.rationale: The inverted Korean phrasing intensifies the single realization that Jin is approaching; his actual arrival follows afterward.

findings.current: At Lee Jungryong’s state funeral, there had been a new Head of Security standing beside Go Jun like a shadow.
findings.defect: The binding glossary requires 국가장 to be rendered as “national funeral,” not “state funeral.”
findings.rationale: This is an exact established terminology match in the supplied glossary.
findings.replacement: At Lee Jungryong’s national funeral, there had been a new Head of Security standing beside Go Jun like a shadow.
findings.source: 이정룡의 국가장이 치러지던 그때, 석고준의 곁을 그림자처럼 지키던 새로운 경호팀장.

findings.current: Go Jun had been protected by a fence made from two words: the rule of law.
findings.defect: The source refers to the two syllables or characters of 법치, whereas the English phrase “the rule of law” is not two words.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves the source’s explicit quantitative image without making a false claim about the English phrase.
findings.replacement: Go Jun had been protected by a fence built from the two-syllable Korean term for the rule of law.
findings.source: 당시의 석고준은 법치(法治)라는 두 글자로 만들어진 울타리 속에 있었으니까.

findings.current: “The target is moving alone! One hundred third floor! No—he’s entered the one hundred fourth!”
findings.defect: The floor numbers are rendered with ungrammatical English ordinals, and the first report lacks the verb needed in natural English.
findings.rationale: The replacement naturally conveys the rapidly updated floor report without changing the target’s movement.
findings.replacement: “The target is moving alone! He’s on the 103rd floor! No—he’s entered the 104th!”

findings.current: “One hundred nineteenth floor! The target has broken through the one hundred nineteenth floor!”
findings.defect: Both instances use malformed English ordinal phrasing.
findings.rationale: English floor numbers require the ordinal form “119th.”
findings.replacement: “The 119th floor! The target has broken through the 119th floor!”

summary: One critical subject reversal, one added arrival beat, one binding terminology mismatch, one inaccurate rendering of the source’s two-syllable phrasing, and two malformed floor ordinals.
